products.body_html:
The Hooga Red Light Therapy Mat for Dogs & Pets

A full-body light therapy mat built for your dog or cat, not adapted from a human panel. The Hooga Red Light Therapy Mat (Model HG-BE980) is soft, flexible, and lays flat on the floor, in a crate, or on a pet bed — giving your pet a familiar surface to rest on during a session.

Across its 40.2″ × 24.0″ surface, 980 dual-chip LEDs deliver 660 nm red light and 850 nm near-infrared light in the same LED position, so both wavelengths are distributed evenly across the mat rather than alternating position to position.

Three Light Modes, Five Brightness Levels, Four Timers

The inline controller gives you real control over how a session runs:

  • Modes: RED+NIR together, RED only, or NIR only. Near-infrared light is nearly invisible to the eye, so the mat looks dim in NIR mode even though it is working normally.
  • Brightness: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, or 100%.
  • Timer: 10, 15, 20, or 25 minutes with automatic shutoff.
  • Pulse: continuous, or 10 Hz / 40 Hz pulsed output.

At startup the mat defaults to RED+NIR, 100% brightness, 15 minutes, pulse off. Every setting is one button press away on the controller.

Built for Pets, Not Repurposed From a Panel

There is no rigid frame to position, no complicated setup, and no battery to charge. The mat runs on the supplied AC power adapter (input 100–240 V AC, 50/60 Hz; output 32 V DC, 96 W) and includes built-in over-temperature protection. It lays flat, folds loosely for storage, and stays quiet during sessions so your pet can settle in.

How to Introduce the Mat

  1. Place the mat flat on a dry, stable indoor surface with the LEDs facing up. Avoid soft, springy surfaces that let the mat bend.
  2. Start at 20% brightness for 10 minutes while your pet becomes familiar with the mat. Stay with your pet the whole session.
  3. If your pet is relaxed and comfortable, increase brightness or session time gradually.
  4. For general wellness, start with three to five sessions per week and use no more than once daily unless your veterinarian directs otherwise.

Common Ways Pet Owners Use It

Pet owners include red and near-infrared light sessions in general wellness routines focused on everyday comfort, relaxation, and post-activity recovery. The full-body format suits active and working dogs, senior-pet wellness routines, and everyday at-home sessions for dogs, cats, and other animal companions.

Important Safety Information

  • Supervise every session and let your pet leave the mat freely.
  • Keep the mat, controller, adapter, and cords dry, and use them indoors only.
  • Do not stare into the LEDs or place them over your pet’s eyes.
  • Do not use damaged equipment or sharply fold, puncture, or crush the mat.
  • Stop the session if your pet moves away, seems uncomfortable, or the mat feels hot.
  • Ask your veterinarian first if your pet is pregnant, recovering from surgery, unwell, or taking photosensitizing medication.

This is a general wellness product and is not a substitute for veterinary care. It is not a medical device and is not intended to diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any condition.

The Hooga Red Light PEMF Mat

The Hooga Red Light PEMF Mat is a full-body wellness mat that stacks three therapies into one session — pulsed electromagnetic fields, red and near-infrared light, and far-infrared heat — so you can relax, recover, and recharge without switching between devices.

It's the same PEMF + far-infrared platform we've built our reputation on, upgraded with 150 red and near-infrared LEDs (75 red at 630/660nm and 75 near-infrared at 810/850nm) embedded along the length of the mat, plus a a preset range of 0.9–45 Hz with 0.1–100 Hz manual mode and 14 preset programs. It's for the person who wants light therapy, PEMF, and infrared heat in a single all-in-one full-body session — no separate panel, no separate mat.

Three Therapies, One Session

Most PEMF mats give you PEMF and heat. Red light panels give you photons. This mat brings all three together, so a single 20-minute session covers what would otherwise require two or three separate devices.

  • PEMF — 6 evenly distributed copper coils, 0.9–45 Hz preset range (0.1–100 Hz in manual mode), 14 preset programs plus manual mode
  • Red & Near-Infrared Light — 150 total LEDs (75 red at 630/660nm, 75 NIR at 810/850nm) with independent on/off controls
  • Far-Infrared Heat — adjustable from 86°F to 140°F with configurable timer

What Is PEMF Therapy?

PEMF stands for Pulsed Electromagnetic Field therapy. Every cell in your body carries an electrical charge. Over time, stress, poor sleep, and everyday wear can leave cells under-charged. PEMF delivers gentle, low-frequency electromagnetic pulses — similar to the Earth's own natural magnetic field — that support your body's cellular processes. It's the same technology used in professional wellness clinics, chiropractic offices, and sports recovery centers worldwide.

14 Preset Programs, Grouped by Purpose

The digital controller ships with 14 preset programs (P1–P14) organized around brainwave ranges and use case:

  • Energize (P2, P5, P6, P7) — higher-frequency Beta/Gamma programs for daytime alertness and energy
  • Focus & Reset (P4, P8, P11) — Alpha/Beta blends for calm focus
  • Relax (P3, P9) — mid-range Alpha for stress reduction and unwinding
  • Sleep (P12, P13, P14) — Delta programs for rest and deep sleep; P14 runs a full 7 hours for all-night use
  • Grounding (P1) — 7.83 Hz Schumann Resonance, 7-hour 20-minute session
  • Meditation (P10) — Theta program for meditation practice

You can also enter manual mode and dial in any frequency from 0.1–100 Hz. Frequency bands: Delta 0.9–4 Hz, Theta 4–8 Hz, Alpha 8–12 Hz, Beta 12–30 Hz, Gamma 30–45 Hz.

Red & Near-Infrared Light — Built In

Two dedicated photon buttons on the controller give you independent control over the light system:

  • Photon 1 (Red) — 75 LEDs delivering 630nm and 660nm red light, commonly associated with surface tissue and skin
  • Photon 2 (Near-Infrared) — 75 LEDs delivering 810nm and 850nm near-infrared light, which penetrates deeper into tissue

Run red only, near-infrared only, or both. Each light program runs 2 hours. Because the LEDs are embedded along the length of the mat, exposure is full-body rather than localized to one panel-sized area.

Why PEMF, Light, and Heat Work Better Together

Far-infrared heat penetrates deeper than a conventional heating pad, warming tissue from the inside out. Red and near-infrared light deliver photons at wavelengths cells are able to absorb. PEMF layers on gentle electromagnetic pulses. When you stack all three in a single session, you get a full-body experience no single-modality device can match.

  • Universal power adapter: 100–240V, 50/60Hz — works worldwide with the appropriate plug
  • Auto shut-off: 12-hour idle safety cutoff

How is this different from the standard Hooga PEMF Mat?

The standard Hooga PEMF Mat with Infrared Heat is $899 and gives you PEMF plus far-infrared heat. If you want light therapy without buying a separate panel, this is the mat for you.

Can I use PEMF, light, and heat separately?

Yes. The three systems are independently controlled from the S70PVA controller. You can run any single therapy alone, any combination, or all three at once during a single session.

The mat ships with 14 preset programs grouped by purpose — Energize (Beta/Gamma), Focus & Reset, Relax (Alpha), Sleep (Delta), Grounding (7.83 Hz Schumann), and Meditation (Theta). How long is a red-light session?

Each light program runs 2 hours. You can run red only (Photon 1), near-infrared only (Photon 2), or both together. Most people start with 10–15 minute sessions and adjust from there.

products.title: Hooga Luma LED Red Light Therapy Mask

Meet the Hooga Luma LED Red Light Therapy Mask — a fully wireless, rechargeable LED face mask with 280 LEDs across 5 light modes. No external controller box, no dangling cable during your session. Power it on directly from the mask, switch modes with the included wireless remote, and run an entire treatment hands-free.

Designed for daily at-home skincare, the Luma delivers red, near-infrared, blue, blue+red, and green wavelengths in 5-minute auto-timed sessions — a clinically-relevant dose range with the convenience of a built-in battery. The Luma is FDA 510(k) cleared (K253712) as an over-the-counter Class II medical device for adults in home use.

✅ FDA 510(k) Cleared – Class II medical device, clearance number K253712.
✅ Completely Wireless – 2,000mAh battery built into the mask. No controller box on a cord.
✅ 5 Dedicated Light Modes – red, red + near-infrared, blue, blue + red, and green.
✅ 280 LEDs – even, full-face coverage with an auto 5-minute timer and automatic shutoff.
✅ Two Ways to Control – on-mask power button plus an included wireless remote.
✅ Lightweight & Cordless – just 11.6 oz, USB-C rechargeable with ~24 sessions per charge.

The 5 Light Therapy Modes

Each mode runs for an auto-timed 5-minute session and shuts off on its own. Short-press the power button on the mask (or the M button on the remote) to cycle through:

Mode Wavelength Irradiance Dose (5 min)
M1 — Red 630 nm 38 mW/cm² 11.4 J/cm²
M2 — Red + Near Infrared 630 + 850 nm 45 mW/cm² 13.5 J/cm²
M3 — Blue 465 nm 29 mW/cm² 8.7 J/cm²
M4 — Blue + Red 465 + 630 nm 48 mW/cm² 14.4 J/cm²
M5 — Green 525 nm 36 mW/cm² 10.8 J/cm²

When to Use Each Mode

  • M1 Red (630 nm) — Everyday anti-aging session. A good default starting mode for the appearance of fine lines, uneven tone, and a tired-looking complexion.
  • M2 Red + Near Infrared (630 + 850 nm) — Deeper rejuvenation. Pairs visible red with near-infrared, which penetrates further into the skin. Designed to support mature or stressed skin and post-workout recovery feel.
  • M3 Blue (465 nm) — Targeted clarifying session for blemish-prone or congested-looking skin. Skip if you'd rather not expose your skin to blue light.
  • M4 Blue + Red (465 + 630 nm) — Combination session. Pairs the clarifying feel of blue with the rejuvenating feel of red — a good choice for blemish-prone areas plus overall tone in the same routine.
  • M5 Green (525 nm) — Even-tone and calming session. Often used for the appearance of dark spots, uneven pigmentation, and visible redness.

FDA 510(k) Clearance

The Hooga Luma is an FDA 510(k)-cleared Class II medical device — clearance number K253712 — for over-the-counter home use by adults. This is the same premarket clearance pathway required for professional-grade LED masks sold in dermatology offices and premium beauty retailers.

Cleared indications for use:

What’s Inside

How People Use It

  • Back and shoulders: Lie flat with the mat under your back. The spike pressure targets tension along the spine while red and NIR light reach the skin and near-surface tissue.
  • Feet, legs, or arms: Stand or press against the mat to work localized areas. Adjust pressure with a thin shirt or towel to start.
  • Wind-down routine: Many customers use it as an end-of-day habit. The pressure is stimulating for the first minute or two, then relaxing as your body adapts.
  • Warmup before stretching: A short session before mobility or yoga can loosen tension in the back.

New to Acupressure? Start Here

  1. First session: Wear a thin shirt to reduce initial intensity. Lie down for 5–10 minutes rather than a full 15.
  2. Sessions 2–5: Extend toward the full 15 minutes. The sharpness fades within the first couple of minutes as your body adjusts.
  3. Ongoing: Skin-to-mat contact delivers the full effect. Many users work down to a bare-skin session after a week.

How to Use

  1. Connect the timer control cable to the mat, then to the power supply cable.
  2. Plug the power supply into an outlet — the mat is now in standby.
  3. Lie down on the mat, then press the timer button once to start the 15-minute session.
  4. The lights turn on and the indicator illuminates. Timer beeps at the end, lights turn off, and the mat returns to standby.
  5. Unplug from the outlet when not in use.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does the mat produce heat?
No — this mat delivers red / near-infrared light and acupressure only. It does not have a heating element. If you’re looking for infrared heat therapy, see our Infrared Sauna Blanket.

Does it really have 3,000+ spikes?
Yes — 3,024 exactly. 144 discs across the mat, each disc has 21 firm plastic spikes.

Is the spike sensation supposed to hurt?
The first minute or two can feel sharp, especially with bare skin. That’s normal for acupressure. Most people find the sensation shifts to warm, tingly, or relaxed once the body adjusts. Start with a thin shirt if the initial contact is too intense.

Can I use it every day?
Yes — daily 15-minute sessions are fine for most people. Skip a day if your back feels sore from a session and let it recover.

How do I clean it?
Wipe with a damp cloth or non-toxic disinfectant spray after use. Avoid soaking or harsh chemicals on the fabric backing.

Can I use it during pregnancy or with a medical condition?
Talk to your healthcare provider first. Acupressure and light exposure aren’t automatically contraindicated, but individual circumstances vary.

The Hooga Red Light Therapy Laser Helmet is an at-home low-level laser therapy (LLLT) device designed for people who want to support hair health and scalp wellness with a consistent daily routine. Featuring 96 laser diodes emitting 650±5nm red light, the helmet delivers focused laser light directly to your scalp during convenient 10-minute sessions. An intelligent sensor system pauses the session if the head moves out of position and resumes when repositioned. The lightweight 1.41 lb body and compact 10.5 x 7.9 x 5.8 inch profile make it easy to use anywhere in your home.

Hooga is positioned as a wellness device at a fraction of the price of FDA-cleared laser helmets — see the comparison below for an honest side-by-side against the best-known clinic-grade options.

How Red Light Laser Therapy May Support Hair Health

Low-level laser therapy (LLLT) in the 630–680nm range has been studied at the category level for its effects on scalp tissue and hair follicles. The general mechanism researchers point to is photobiomodulation — low-power light energy is absorbed by cells, where it may support normal cellular activity in tissues like the scalp.

The Hooga Laser Helmet is built around this category of light therapy. It is a wellness device, not a medical device, and is not FDA-cleared to treat hair loss. Individual results vary. What it offers is a hands-free, sit-and-go way to make a daily 10-minute laser light therapy routine part of your scalp care — without booking clinic appointments or wearing a heavy corded helmet.

How It Works

The Hooga Laser Helmet emits a precise 650±5nm wavelength — the wavelength range most commonly referenced in at-home laser scalp devices — through 96 individual laser diodes positioned across the inside of the helmet. Each diode is rated at 5mW and the device meets Class II safety standards for at-home use.

A built-in motion sensor system monitors head position throughout your session. If the helmet detects movement out of the session zone, it automatically pauses; reposition it and the session resumes where you left off. After 10 continuous minutes of light exposure, the helmet signals session completion.

How the Hooga Laser Helmet Compares

Frequently Asked Questions

Is the Hooga Laser Helmet FDA-cleared for hair loss?
No. The Hooga Laser Helmet is a wellness device, not a medical device. Devices like iRestore Professional, Capillus, and Theradome are FDA-cleared for treatment of androgenetic alopecia; Hooga is not. We don't claim to treat, cure, or prevent hair loss.

How is this different from a $1,000+ FDA-cleared device?
The main difference is regulatory: FDA clearance allows other brands to make specific medical claims about hair regrowth that we can't make. On hardware, the Hooga helmet uses 96 laser diodes at 650±5nm — comparable wavelength range to leading cleared devices. The Hooga also includes smart auto-pause sensors and a cordless USB-C design that several pricier helmets don't have. The price difference reflects the regulatory pathway, not necessarily the underlying laser output.

How long until I see results?
Individual experiences vary widely. At-home laser light therapy is built around consistency over months, not weeks. We don't make specific timing claims. Most published research on LLLT and hair uses daily or every-other-day sessions over 16+ weeks.

How long is each session?
Each session is 10 minutes. The helmet runs an auto-cycle and signals when it's complete.

How often should I use it?
Most at-home laser device routines are built around daily 10-minute sessions. Consistency matters more than session length — pick a time of day you can stick to.

650 ± 5 nm, delivered through 96 individual laser diodes. This wavelength range is the one most commonly referenced in at-home laser scalp devices.

We're not in a position to give medical advice on combining therapies. Many people use at-home light therapy alongside other hair-health routines. Ask a qualified healthcare provider about your specific situation.

Is it safe?
The helmet is built to Class II safety standards with low-power 5mW diodes designed for at-home use. As with any wellness device, if you have a scalp condition or other health concern, speak with a qualified healthcare provider before starting.

Do I need eye protection?
The helmet directs light at your scalp and is enclosed in the helmet body. Follow the included user manual for any specific guidance.

Can I move around during a session?
Small movements are fine — the smart sensor will pause the session if your head moves out of the session zone and resume when you reposition. For best results, stay relatively still.

1.41 lbs (about 640 grams). It's one of the lighter helmet-style devices on the market and is designed to be comfortable to wear for the full 10-minute session.

Red Light Therapy Blanket vs. Red Light Therapy Bag: One Product, Two Use Cases

Customers shop for this category under several names — red light therapy blanket, red light therapy bag, infrared blanket, red light sleeping bag — and they're all describing the same idea: a wearable, full-body alternative to a wall-mounted panel. The Hooga blanket is built to work both ways:

  • As a blanket (unzipped flat): Lay it on a bed, couch, or yoga mat and rest face-up or face-down. Best for targeted front- or back-of-body sessions, stretching, or post-workout recovery.
  • As a bag (zipped closed): Climb inside for a 360° wraparound session. The front and back panels surround your torso, hips, and legs simultaneously, so you get full coverage without flipping.

Most users alternate between the two modes depending on the goal — bag mode for full-body wellness sessions, blanket mode for focused recovery on a specific area.

Wall-mounted panels are excellent for targeted work, but they ask you to stand still, rotate, and re-position to cover your whole body. A red light therapy blanket eliminates that overhead:

  • Travel-friendly. Folds down to fit alongside other gear, unlike a 4-foot panel.
  • Daily-use comfortable. Soft neoprene against the skin, not a hard panel surface.

If your routine involves consistent, full-body sessions — recovery after training, evening wind-down, daily wellness — a blanket reduces friction. If you mostly want targeted face or joint exposure, a panel may still be the better fit.

  4. Stay consistent. Red light therapy is a daily-habit tool, not a one-shot fix. Most users run sessions 4–7 days per week.
  5. Clean between sessions. Wipe the inner neoprene surface with a soft, lightly damp cloth as needed.

Both. It's a single device that unzips flat into a blanket/mat or zips closed into a wraparound bag. You pick the mode based on the session.

2,680 LEDs total — 1,400 on the back panel and 1,280 on the front. Each LED is a triple-chip bead (two near-infrared + one red), so the effective chip count is meaningfully higher than the LED count alone.

0.14 V/m — low EMF output, measured at the surface during operation.

The controller includes a built-in timer. Most users run 10–20 minute sessions, daily or several times per week. Adjust based on your goals and how your body responds.
